A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TOTO model and BOOM benchmark. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original TOTO forecasting evaluations, fine-tuning results, architectural ablations, and analyses of BOOM.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds computational-efficiency measurements and further BOOMLET comparisons.

M1.justification: The architecture, causal scaling, proportional attention, Student-T mixture head, composite loss, and forecasting procedure remain unchanged. V2 documents KV caching in the efficiency study without establishing that it was newly introduced.

E1.justification: V2 adds controlled synthetic multivariate workloads for computational evaluation in Appendix D.4. The real-world forecasting coverage remains BOOM/BOOMLET, GIFT-Eval, and the same six LSF datasets; the pretraining sources are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 11 add DLinear and DeepAR comparisons on BOOMLET, with no corresponding full-BOOM results. Tables 12–14 add Time-MoE-Large to the stratified comparisons, although that model already appeared in v1's aggregate evaluation. The principal existing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix D.4 introduces a distinct profiling protocol: single-output-sample forecasting on an A100 40 GB, context 2048, horizon 480, eight variate counts, four computational metrics, and cache-on/off controls. Separately, C.3 revises BOOMLET's sampling description to prioritize queries with more variates. These reported changes do not establish that the existing forecasting evaluations were rerun; the LSF stride description remains unchanged.

E4.justification: The new D.4 study systematically examines computational scaling with input cardinality and the effect of disabling KV caching, adding substantive evidence about efficiency. The original component ablations in Appendix E, near-constant-series analysis, and qualitative forecasting cases are retained.

E5.justification: V2 Table 18 introduces plus/minus uncertainty entries for computational measurements. It does not define those quantities or disclose repetition counts or seeds. Existing forecast prediction intervals are unchanged, and forecasting-score uncertainty reporting is not expanded.

E6.justification: V2 adds the computational results and DLinear/DeepAR BOOMLET scores. BOOMLET ranks change alongside the expanded comparison, including TOTO's 1.244 to 1.300 in Table 2. Table 11 revises Moirai-Small's BOOM MASE/CRPS from 0.738/0.447 to 0.729/0.442. TOTO's Electricity zero-shot MAE/MSE changes from 0.242/0.158 to 0.243/0.161, with related fine-tuned and horizon-specific revisions. The headline BOOM and GIFT-Eval TOTO scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The complexity derivation, normalization equations, mixture-model formulation, and loss definitions are retained. Describing epsilon as a small positive constant instead of machine epsilon clarifies numerical terminology without adding substantive mathematical reasoning or a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: the observability-focused TOTO foundation model, BOOM benchmark, large pretraining corpus, and state-of-the-art forecasting claims. The efficiency study supports the existing scalability motivation without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: D.4 adds interpretations of computational scalability and explicitly limits the study to single-sample forward computations, excluding test-time sampling costs. It also acknowledges differing KV-cache support. Its claim of lowest or second-lowest wall time across all variate counts overstates Table 18, where Moirai and TimesFM both outperform standard TOTO at 10 and 50 variates.

D1.justification: V2 documents profiling hardware, model variants, and KV-cache use. A.6 removes the conflicting 65-trial statement and clarifies 133 tuning iterations of 50,000 steps each, without demonstrating increased computation. The abstract adds a BOOM dataset reference but introduces malformed prefixes in the repository and dataset links; the existing open-source release claim is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Gao et al.'s UniTS to the factorized-attention references. The broader research positioning is retained. The expanded main-text comparison with Moirai's mixture distribution largely repeats information already present in v1 Appendix A.3.

P1.justification: There are localized wording, terminology, and cross-reference edits, an added author, and the new D.4 subsection. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact, with no extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 moves the detailed zero-shot LSF comparison from v1 Table 15 into main-text Table 4, expands BOOM tables with comparator columns and rank rows, and adds the efficiency table. Figure labels, colors, captions, and placement receive limited revisions; the existing visual analyses are retained.

improvement.justification: The added efficiency study, including cache-off controls, provides useful empirical support for scalability, and the BOOMLET comparisons broaden the evidence base. The improvement is limited by undefined uncertainty quantities, an overstated wall-time summary in D.4, and malformed resource links. The core forecasting evidence and methodological contribution remain largely unchanged.
